cues.en: — has a COP of 1.

cues.zh: 这意味着每消耗 1 千瓦电力，就会产生 1 千瓦的热量输出。

cues.en: Turning electrical energy into heat is 100% efficient,

cues.zh: 所以这个取暖器消耗的每一瓦电，最终都以热量形式留在了房间里。
cues.en: so every single watt of power that this heater is consuming is ending up in the room as heat.

cues.zh: 这不算差，但有个小问题是，发电本身 A)
cues.en: That’s not bad, but a wrinkle there is that electricity *generation* is A)

cues.en: not 100% efficient and B)

cues.en: somewhat scarce.

cues.en: Let’s start with efficiency - a modern power plant that burns natural gas is, after transmission losses,

cues.zh: 效率大约只有40%。
cues.en: about 40% efficient.

cues.en: If you burn natural gas at a rate of 10 megawatts,

cues.en: a power plant will only produce 4 megawatts of electricity from it.

cues.zh: 虽然这些电通入几千台电暖器后，也只会变成大约4兆瓦的热量，
cues.en: While that would get turned into about 4 megawatts of heat if it was run through a few thousand space heaters,

cues.zh: 但如果我们把这种天然气通过管道送入建筑，就能把它变成超过9兆瓦的热量
cues.en: we could turn that into more than 9 megawatts of heat if we piped that gas into buildings

cues.en: and burned it locally in boilers or furnaces.

cues.zh: 正如我在关于炉具的视频中探讨过的，
cues.en: As I explored in my video on furnaces,

cues.zh: 我们知道如何以安全、有效的方式，把燃料几乎全部的热能提取出来。
cues.en: we know how to get nearly all of a fuel’s heat energy out of it in a safe, effective fashion.

cues.zh: 所以……在世界很多地方，我们正是这么做的。
cues.en: So… in many parts of the world that’s exactly what we do.

cues.zh: 直到不久之前，现场燃烧燃料一直是
cues.en: Burning fuel on-site has been until pretty recently

cues.zh: 利用这种资源来供暖的最合理方式。
cues.en: the most rational way to use that resource for the purpose of space heating.

cues.zh: 像烤面包机那样的电加热还有另一个问题，
cues.en: The other problem with electric heat a la toasters

cues.zh: 就是电网容量有限，没法到处都满足。
cues.en: is that there is only so much grid capacity to go around.

cues.zh: 给一栋建筑供暖需要大量能源——
cues.en: It takes a lot of energy to heat a building -

cues.zh: 建筑供暖是我们最耗能的事情之一。
cues.en: heating buildings is among the most energy-intensive things we do.

cues.zh: 而且在很多地区，电网规模根本不足以让所有人都改用简单的电取暖。
cues.en: And in many areas the electric grid just isn’t big enough to switch everyone over to simple electric heat.

cues.zh: 说清楚一点，这并不是因为我们建不出足够大的电网。
cues.en: And it’s not because we couldn’t build it to do so, to be clear.

cues.zh: 只是，除了那些能获得丰富稳定可再生能源（比如水电）的地区之外，
cues.en: It’s just that, except in areas with access to abundant and stable renewable energy like hydroelectric power,

cues.zh: 传统上用电取暖要贵得多，也更耗费资源，
cues.en: it has traditionally been much more expensive and resource intensive to heat with electricity

cues.zh: 因为化石燃料发电厂存在效率难题。
cues.en: because of the efficiency challenges in fossil-fuel power plants.

cues.zh: 在我居住的这类地区，电力基础设施
cues.en: The electric infrastructure in areas like where I live

cues.zh: 在冬季预计根本发不了那么多电，因为历史上电力需求会在
cues.en: just isn't expected to produce as much much energy in winter months because electricity demand has historically fallen

cues.zh: 空调停转、暖气炉点火时下降。
cues.en: when air conditioners stop running and furnaces fire up.

cues.zh: 但多亏了热泵，我们基本上可以一并绕开这两个挑战。
cues.en: But, thanks to heat pumps, we can largely sidestep both of those challenges altogether.

cues.zh: 就发电需求而言，
cues.en: When it comes to the need for electricity generation,

cues.zh: 因为热泵并不是把电能转化成热
cues.en: since heat pumps aren’t converting electrical energy into heat

cues.zh: 而是用它驱动制冷回路，把热量搬进室内，
cues.en: but are instead using it to drive a refrigeration circuit which moves heat indoors,

cues.zh: 它们的性能系数大于 1。
cues.en: they have coefficients of performance that are greater than 1.

cues.zh: 简单说，同样的电，它们比普通电暖器产生更多有用热量。
cues.en: Simply put, they produce more useful heat with the same electricity than a simple electric heater does.

cues.zh: 有时甚至超过 5 倍。
cues.en: Sometimes, more than 5 times as much.

cues.zh: 这意味着，虽然热泵会给电网带来更大需求
cues.en: This means that although heat pumps will put more demand on the electric grid

cues.zh: 在目前用燃气取暖的地区
cues.en: in places that currently use gas for heating,

cues.zh: 但它们所需的能量只是电阻加热的一小部分
cues.en: they require a fraction of the energy of resistive heat

cues.zh: 因此在世界那些地区，电气化变得可行得多。
cues.en: and so make electrification much more feasible in those parts of the world.

cues.zh: 这当然很好，但接下来还有更妙的地方。
cues.en: That’s definitely good, but here’s where things get even better.

cues.zh: 我敢说，简直令人惊叹。
cues.en: Dare I say, mind-blowing.

cues.zh: 还记得吗，我们可以把天然气管道接入建筑并在那里燃烧
cues.en: Remember that we can pipe natural gas into a building and burn it there,

cues.zh: 这几十年来一直如此
cues.en: as we’ve been doing for decades,

cues.zh: 我们大概能将其95%的能量以热的形式捕获。
cues.en: and we can capture perhaps 95% of its energy as heat.

cues.zh: 但如果我们不这么做，而是在发电厂燃烧它来发电
cues.en: But if instead of doing that we burned it in a power plant to make electricity,

cues.zh: 热泵就能大显神通了。
cues.en: heat pumps will work their magic.

cues.zh: 我们可能只能把40%的天然气能量转化为电能
cues.en: We may only get 40% of the gas’s energy turned into electricity,

cues.zh: 但当你用它驱动一台COP为5的热泵时
cues.en: but when you use it to run a heat pump operating with a COP of 5,

cues.zh: 最终你的实际效率相当于200%。
cues.en: in the end you’re effectively operating at 200% efficiency.

cues.zh: 相比在炉子或锅炉中以完美效率燃烧天然气，这相当于多出100%的能量。
cues.en: That’s a 100% bonus compared to burning the gas in a furnace or boiler with perfect efficiency.

cues.zh: 用这种方式，实际送进建筑里的能量比天然气本身所含的还多，
cues.en: Literally more energy than the gas itself contains ends up getting put into buildings when you use it this way,

cues.zh: 这简直太惊人了！
cues.en: and that’s nothing short of amazing!

cues.zh: 当然，我敢肯定某些老顽固正对着屏幕大声嚷嚷，

cues.zh: 但它们的COP只需达到2.5，就能与现场燃烧燃料打平。
cues.en: But, they only need to operate with a COP of 2.5 to break even with on-site fuel combustion.

cues.zh: 这会把天然气发电厂中获得的40%
cues.en: That turns the 40% captured in a natural gas power plant

cues.zh: 直接变回100%——甚至略胜最高效的炉子一筹。
cues.en: right back into 100% - eking out even the most efficient furnaces.

cues.en: And, here’s why this video’s happening,

cues.en: that is actually very, very attainable.

cues.en: With simple air source heat pumps.

cues.en: Even in cold climates.

cues.en: landed at or below 5 degrees.
